00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick round robin intro and then dive into the access and staging handoff, we have about 45 minutes, friendly reminder i'll try to keep timestamps short.

00:52 Tom Anders: we prefer in our VPC for now, because we need to validate routing and our ingress rules, also because of egress cost tracking. we can open a dedicated subnet for the pilot.
01:03 Maya Chen: understood. we'll need a couple of things from you: CIDR blocks, security group asymps, and a bastion IP. elena, i'll hand it to you for the technical specifics.
01:12 Elena Soto: yeah for the runtime we'll need outbound HTTPS to redwood endpoints, also inbound from the bastion for SSH into the staging nodes — and we recommend a minimum of two GPU instances for the pilot to exercise autoscaling.
01:26 Tom Anders: okay GPU nodes are fine, the thing is we've got constrained quota on the region, might need to request a quota bump.

01:40 Priya Nair: quick Q on data in transit — do you support customer-managed KMS or do you require Redwood's KMS for the private deploy? there's often procurement constraints.
01:52 Elena Soto: we support both. for Private/VPC we'll typically suggest customer-managed KMS for full key control; hosted uses Redwood KMS by default. we'll document the keywrap and envelope flow in the runbook.
02:03 Priya Nair: perfect, can you include details around key rotation and audit logs? we need to show auditors.
02:08 Ravi Patel: absolutely, priya. we'll include which logs are emitted and how to pull them into your SIEM. will also include recommended retention.
02:15 Alicia Gomez: what about PII and telemetry — we need to ensure prompt logs aren't stored beyond our retention policy.
02:20 Elena Soto: there is an option to disable full transcript logging for the pilot — we can switch to token-only metrics and structured response capture. note: that reduces observability for debugging but improves compliance surface.
02:34 Tom Anders: on networking, we have to maintain strict egress through our NAT devices. can the redwood runtime sit behind our NAT?
02:40 Maya Chen: yes, the runtime can be deployed in customer VPC and will egress via your NAT as long as outbound rules allow the endpoints. we'll add a checklist item for IP ranges and FQDNs to whitelist.
02:53 Tom Anders: ok good.

03:24 Alicia Gomez: we want under 1s for 95th for the initial test, really the baseline is cost per 1k tokens and latency tradeoff. we also want no errors over 24 hours of continuous runs.
03:35 Elena Soto: good, i'll craft the test harness to log errors and raw token counts. i'll also stitch in trace ids so you can map requests back into your logs.
03:44 Tom Anders: do we have recommendations on quantization? we've got a lower-cost constraint.
03:49 Elena Soto: for cost optimization we can use 4-bit quantized variants in staging; there will be a small quality delta. we'll provide A/B sample prompts in the playbook so you can evaluate tradeoffs.

04:15 Priya Nair: good. can you also share the data processing addendum?
